clue.text: Richard is shaky

definitions.meaning: a pet form of the name Richard, like Dick
informal British for weak or unreliable, as in a heart that is not sound

explanation.surface: A man named Richard is feeling unsteady.
explanation.definitionFit: The pet name sits beside the British slang adjective for unsound or wobbly, as in a bad knee.

clue.text: Challenged sin, being reckless

parts.note: dared means challenged someone to do something
evil is wickedness or sin

explanation.surface: Someone was provoked into wrongdoing while acting recklessly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being' is a link joining wordplay and definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A daredevil is someone recklessly bold, and the word works as an adjective meaning rash.

clue.text: Protection of original work. but imitation OK?

parts.note: a copy is an imitation
right means correct or OK

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether copying is acceptable given legal safeguards on creative work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'but' is a link; the joke is that copying is exactly what the protection forbids.
explanation.definitionFit: The legal right to control the reproduction of an author's or artist's creations.

clue.text: American is a jerk

definitions.meaning: informal word for a person from the United States
a sudden sharp pull or tug

explanation.surface: A remark that an American is an obnoxious person.
explanation.definitionFit: A US citizen in slang, and a sharp tug as a noun or verb.

clue.text: There and back, or circuitous journey?

definitions.meaning: a journey out to a place and home again
a trip that goes in a circle, the question mark flagging the playful reading

explanation.surface: A traveller wonders whether an out-and-home outing counts as a loop.
explanation.definitionFit: A return journey, out and home, can also be read as a tour travelling in a circle.

clue.text: Agitator who always returns to the same point?

definitions.meaning: a political firebrand stirring up rebellion

definitions.text: who always returns to the same point?
definitions.meaning: something that keeps going round and round, completing turns

explanation.surface: A rebel is mocked as someone who keeps coming back to the same argument.
explanation.definitionFit: A rebel overthrowing the state, and something rotating in full circles, back where it started.

clue.text: To be silent is stupid

explanation.surface: A saying that keeping quiet is foolish.
explanation.definitionFit: Mute or speechless in one sense, slow-witted or foolish in another.

clue.text: Managed to get central heating for farm

parts.note: ran means managed, as in running a business

explanation.surface: Someone succeeded in having central heating installed on their farm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to get' and 'for' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: A ranch is a large farm, especially one raising cattle in the Americas.

clue.text: False coin used to deceive

parts.note: P is a penny, a British coin

indicators.note: to deceive is to mislead, so the letters are disguised in a misleading order

explanation.surface: A counterfeit penny is passed to trick someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'False' reads as an anagram signal but is the definition; 'to deceive' is the anagram indicator, and P is a British penny.
explanation.definitionFit: Pseud is British informal for sham or pretentious, describing someone affecting intellectual airs.

clue.text: Come of age in US state prison

parts.note: RI is the postal abbreviation for Rhode Island
pen is short for penitentiary, a prison

explanation.surface: Someone reaches adulthood while locked up in an American jail.
explanation.definitionFit: To mature or become fully developed, as fruit or a person does with time.

clue.text: Force very English virile types to church

parts.note: he-men are macho, virile fellows
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: An order to march some very manly Englishmen off to church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is only a link joining the pieces; CE stands for the Church of England.
explanation.definitionFit: Vehemence is forcefulness or great intensity of feeling, so force is a fair synonym.

clue.text: Shrewdly practical, urge some solid protein

parts.note: hard-boiled means tough-minded and unsentimental
to egg someone on is to urge them

explanation.surface: Advice to a hard-headed person to eat something firm and nourishing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'egg on' means to urge; the definition is a whimsical description of a firmly cooked breakfast item.
explanation.definitionFit: An egg cooked until set solid is a portion of protein, so the description fits.

clue.text: About to free king, using dagger

indicators.note: about tells us to turn the word for setting free round the other way

parts.note: to rid is to free or clear
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: Someone means to liberate a monarch by drawing a blade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' looks like a container or 'roughly' but here signals a turnaround; 'using' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A dirk is a short Scottish dagger, traditionally worn with Highland dress.

clue.text: Loud sound of bass real agony

parts.note: B is the music abbreviation for bass

indicators.note: agony suggests the following word is twisted and tortured into a new order

explanation.surface: A deep bass note produces genuine pain in the listener's ears.
explanation.walkthrough: 'agony' is an unusual anagram signal: the letters writhe in pain; B for bass is a music-score convention.
explanation.definitionFit: A blare is a harsh, loud noise, like a trumpet or car horn blasting.

clue.text: Wearing boots, pressing hard into turf

indicators.note: into tells us the abbreviation for hard is pushed inside the word for turf

parts.note: a sod is a piece of turf
H is the pencil-grading abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: Someone in boots presses down hard on the grass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pressing' just joins the surface; 'into' puts H inside SOD.
explanation.definitionFit: Being shod means having footwear on, so someone in boots is literally provided with shoes.

clue.text: Horrid type? Be a good chap!

parts.note: taken as written
ST, for saint, is a crossword convention for a good person

explanation.surface: A plea to a nasty character to behave like a decent fellow.
explanation.walkthrough: ST for saint, a good person, is a common crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: A brute is a horrible, cruel person, as in a nasty piece of work.

clue.text: Object found in Inca village

indicators.note: found in means the answer is sitting within the words that follow

explanation.surface: An artefact turned up in a Peruvian settlement.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across inCA VILlage; 'Object' looks like a noun but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To cavil is to raise petty objections, so to object is a fair verb synonym.

clue.text: Betrothal gets broadcast on very loud tranny

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so these letters are strewn into a new order

explanation.surface: News of an engagement is announced over a blaring radio.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' rearranges the thirteen letters of BETROTHAL GETS; 'tranny' is old British slang for a transistor radio; 'on' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A large portable stereo played at high volume is a booming transistor radio in old slang.

clue.text: Fruit eaten, grin nastily

indicators.note: nastily suggests the letters behave badly and are jumbled up

explanation.surface: Someone eats an orange and smirks maliciously.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nastily' rearranges EATEN GRIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A tangerine is a small orange citrus fruit, a type of mandarin.

clue.text: Stand for show a second time

definitions.meaning: symbolise or act on behalf of
to put on display once more, split after its first two letters as a prefix meaning again

explanation.surface: A request to stand in for someone and stage something again.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition reads the answer as re-present: present again.
explanation.definitionFit: To symbolise or speak on behalf of, and split as re-present to put on display again.

clue.text: In which one crosses one self, ready for yoga

definitions.text: In which one crosses one self, ready for yoga

parts.words: In which one crosses one self, ready for yoga
parts.note: reads like a religious gesture, but describes sitting cross-legged with each foot on the opposite thigh, a classic seated meditation pose

explanation.surface: Someone makes the sign of the cross before a yoga class.
explanation.definitionFit: This seated yoga pose has the legs crossed over each other, feet resting on the thighs.

clue.text: Modest opening — one club

indicators.note: opening means we take only the first letter of the word modest

parts.note: an ace is the one in a pack of cards

explanation.surface: A golfer makes a humble start, holing in one.
explanation.walkthrough: An ace counts as one in cards; 'Modest opening' gives M.
explanation.definitionFit: A mace is a heavy club with a spiked or knobbed head, used as a weapon.

clue.text: Proposes to get funds

explanation.surface: Someone plans to raise money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to get' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Intends as a verb, and money or resources as a noun, as in a man of means.

clue.text: Hiding place for money, say

indicators.note: say means we want a word pronounced the same as the one given

parts.note: cash is ready money

explanation.surface: A secret stash where funds are kept.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A cache is a secret store or hidden stash of goods or valuables.

clue.text: Latitude given to child for confused speech

indicators.note: given to means the abbreviation is attached after the word for a youngster

parts.note: a babe is a baby or young child
L is the abbreviation for latitude on maps

explanation.surface: A youngster is given some leeway for mumbling incoherently.
explanation.walkthrough: 'given to' places the latitude abbreviation after the word for a child.
explanation.definitionFit: A babel is a noisy jumble of voices, after the biblical tower where tongues were confused.

clue.text: Dog may look as you talk

indicators.note: as you talk means we want the spoken form, a word that is pronounced the same

parts.note: to peek is to take a quick look

explanation.surface: A dog might glance at you while you are speaking.
explanation.definitionFit: A peke is short for Pekingese, a small long-haired breed of toy dog.

clue.text: Defeat the finest

definitions.meaning: to get the better of someone

explanation.surface: Beating the top performers.
explanation.definitionFit: To outdo someone as a verb, and top quality as a superlative.

clue.text: Guns are raised to shoot this

definitions.text: Guns are raised to shoot this

indicators.note: in a down clue raised means the word for guns is read upwards

parts.note: gats is old US slang for guns

explanation.surface: Hunters lift their rifles to fire at a deer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'are raised' turns GATS upwards in a down clue; the whole clue also describes deer-hunting.
explanation.definitionFit: A male deer is a quarry for hunters who stalk game on the hills.

clue.text: Cheap tyre remoulded, a typical specimen

indicators.note: a remoulded tyre is reworked, so these letters are reshaped into a new order

explanation.surface: A garage passes off a cut-price retread as a standard example.
explanation.walkthrough: 'remoulded' rearranges CHEAP TYRE; a remould is a retreaded tyre.
explanation.definitionFit: An archetype is the perfect example or model of a kind, a pattern for all others.

clue.text: From ruminant, rip edible part

indicators.note: part means the answer is a portion of the words in front of it

explanation.surface: Advice to tear the good-to-eat portion from a cud-chewing animal.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across ruminanT RIP Edible; the whole clue also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Tripe is the stomach lining of cattle or sheep, an edible part of a cud-chewing animal.

clue.text: Carol hugs Erica, in case

indicators.note: hugs means the word for carol wraps around the plant name

parts.note: to carol is to sing joyfully
Erica is the botanical genus of heaths and heathers

explanation.surface: A girl named Carol embraces her friend Erica, just in case.
explanation.walkthrough: Erica looks like a woman's name but is the heath plant genus; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheathing is a protective covering or casing, as round a cable or a ship's hull.

clue.text: Visitor, the last to leave in gale

indicators.note: in tells us one piece sits inside the word for gale

parts.note: a gust is a sudden strong blast of wind

indicators.note: last means we take only the final letter of the word the

explanation.surface: A guest is the final one to depart while a storm blows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the last' gives E, which goes in GUST; 'to leave' is surface only.
explanation.definitionFit: A guest is a person invited to stay or visit, in someone's house.
